objective: Review and accept the scoped filelist shape-breadth GPU allocation policy dry-run.

review_decision.reason: The dry-run emits deterministic JSON, writes no files, recommends 32x1 with high confidence only for the two reviewed filelist-derived targets, and keeps unknown targets, incomplete source closure, missing repeat-median evidence, 1xN repeated-step workloads, native Verilator support, arbitrary RTL support, and automatic optimal allocation outside the accepted claim.
review_decision.accepted_scope: dry-run policy surface for two reviewed filelist-derived targets
review_decision.weakest_point: The policy is still static and evidence-scoped; it does not parse arbitrary filelists or compute optimal GPU allocation for unreviewed RTL.
known_weaknesses: recommendations are limited to repeat-count-3 evidence for two tracked filelist-derived targets
unknown or incomplete source closure cases are classified but not automatically repaired
1xN repeated-step workloads remain weak without resident or persistent-resident mitigation
native Verilator option integration is not implemented by this gate
no new timing measurement is created by the dry-run

required_next_gate.name: define_filelist_shape_breadth_gpu_allocation_policy_execution_gate
must_pin: whether policy execution means applying the dry-run-selected shape to a tracked template command plan or only producing an operator recommendation
that execution remains limited to reviewed filelist-derived targets unless a broader measurement gate is added
that incomplete source closure must be refused or repaired before any non-dry-run command
that coverage_output_equivalence remains the correctness check for later build/run/compare execution
that runtime, ABI, native Verilator options, and arbitrary RTL optimal allocation remain out of scope

non_claims: not automatic optimal GPU allocation for any design
